device_takeover.reported: Opening the phone app appears to move radio away from desktop; desktop activation can move it back.
device_takeover.mechanism: Lifecycle automatic admission called join even when an own-account reservation already existed. Join rewrote that reservation/presence with a new session. Replacement teardown emitted changes before recording the replacement error, allowing admission to observe an error-free inactive session.
device_takeover.changes: Automatic admission respects current or recently offline own-account reservations. It rechecks after queued admission and profile lookup. Use here explicitly claims the existing own-account place through the existing authorized write. Replacement error is set before teardown notifications. Focus and stale return tickets cannot automatically take the reservation back.
device_takeover.compatibility: Existing single-reservation-per-account data and rule policy retained. No new device fields, trusted device lock or authentication behavior. Same-tab recovery still checks the current server session. Simultaneous first admissions before either snapshot arrives can still race, but no repeated automatic takeover should follow.

media_recovery.behavior: Retain peer entries through failures, negotiate fresh ICE restart offers from either side, resolve collisions by seat ordering and keep unaffected transports intact.
media_recovery.budget_lifetime: Latest local/remote session identity pair. Success and temporary remote presence gaps do not replenish it. Canceled pending retries consume their reserved slot. Explicit reconnect or a new session starts a new budget.
media_recovery.exhaustion: Close only the exhausted peer transport, retain a marker to prevent tick-driven recreation and expose existing Reconnect error/action.
media_recovery.cancellation: Cancel retry/watchdog/gathering waits on departure, local-session change, sign-out and scope disposal. Guard asynchronous negotiation continuations against removed/replaced peers.
media_recovery.bounded_memory: Latest peer history per fixed remote seat, at most nine for a valid local room place. At most four consumed remote offer IDs per history entry. Existing 200-event diagnostics cap retained.
media_recovery.work: At most seven offers and seven answers per fixed identity pair, 14 application signaling writes before SDK transport retries. At room capacity, 24 pairs imply at most 336 application signaling writes for fixed identities, excluding existing presence/floor/cleanup work. No extra queries/listeners or dependency; up to nine peer queues operate concurrently per speaker. Session churn starts additional budgets and is not globally bounded.
